headline: Japan leads Brazil 1-0 at halftime in World Cup clash
summary: Japan takes a surprising early lead against the five-time champions in their round-of-32 knockout match.
details: Japan leads Brazil 1-0 at the end of the first half in their World Cup round-of-32 knockout match. The underdogs have managed to secure a lead against the five-time world champions.
Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti kept an unchanged side from their 3-0 win over Scotland, though 19-year-old Rayan started in place of the injured Raphinha.
Neymar remains on the bench as he continues to recover from a calf injury, with Ancelotti hoping to see him feature later in the game.
Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu made four changes to the starting lineup, opting for a five-man defense to counter the Brazilian attack.
The Japanese side includes Shogo Taniguchi, Takehiro Tomiyasu, and Junya Ito, while Brazil's attack is led by Vinicius Jr and Matheus Cunha.
caption:
A shock lead! Japan is ahead 1-0 at halftime against Brazil in the World Cup knockouts.

Japan leads Brazil 1-0 at the end of the first half in their World Cup round-of-32 knockout match. The underdogs have managed to secure a lead against the five-time world champions.

Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti kept an unchanged side from their 3-0 win over Scotland, though 19-year-old Rayan started in place of the injured Raphinha.

Neymar remains on the bench as he continues to recover from a calf injury, with Ancelotti hoping to see him feature later in the game.

Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu made four changes to the starting lineup, opting for a five-man defense to counter the Brazilian attack.

The Japanese side includes Shogo Taniguchi, Takehiro Tomiyasu, and Junya Ito, while Brazil's attack is led by Vinicius Jr and Matheus Cunha.

headline: ICT to deliver verdict in crimes against humanity case against Inu today
summary: Former information minister and JSD president Hasanul Haq Inu faces judgement over the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July 2024 uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its verdict today against Hasanul Haq Inu, the president of Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD) and former information minister.
Inu, who is currently in jail custody, is the sole accused in a crimes against humanity case linked to the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July 2024 uprising.
The tribunal framed eight charges against him on November 2, 2025, following a probe report submitted by the ICT's investigation agency on September 11 of last year.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that the prosecution expects the tribunal to hand down an appropriate punishment.
However, defence counsel Sifat Mahmud argued that the prosecution failed to prove the charges and expressed hope that the tribunal would acquit Mr. Inu.
A total of 10 prosecution witnesses and two defence witnesses testified before the tribunal before the case was kept pending for judgement.
caption:
Verdict day for Hasanul Haq Inu. The ICT-2 will decide his fate in a crimes against humanity case today.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its verdict today against Hasanul Haq Inu, the president of Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD) and former information minister.

Inu, who is currently in jail custody, is the sole accused in a crimes against humanity case linked to the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July 2024 uprising.

The tribunal framed eight charges against him on November 2, 2025, following a probe report submitted by the ICT's investigation agency on September 11 of last year.

Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that the prosecution expects the tribunal to hand down an appropriate punishment.

However, defence counsel Sifat Mahmud argued that the prosecution failed to prove the charges and expressed hope that the tribunal would acquit Mr. Inu.

A total of 10 prosecution witnesses and two defence witnesses testified before the tribunal before the case was kept pending for judgement.
